notes: Clicked for credits up to 37 credits for many turns without building a rig or contesting remotes, letting the Corp advance and score two Fujii from thinly iced servers. Sat idle again in turns 17-19 while the Corp, needing one point, installed and scored House of Knives via Holo Man.

A coherent NBN tag-and-kill plan that ended in End of the Line, but False Lead and then Tomorrow's Headline went into a remote guarded only by Tsarevna, which has no ETR, and both were stolen. Several draw clicks led to end-of-turn discards, and the many naked trap and asset remotes were mostly trashed cheaply.

Spent almost every turn running unprotected R&D 3-4 times, re-accessing the same top card, while sitting at 0 credits with no economy or rig. Stayed heavily tagged against an NBN deck, took an End of the Line that wiped the grip, and won only because the Corp decked.

Solid scoring-remote play: it advanced Send a Message while the Runner was broke and later built up Server 3 and Server 5 to close out the game. There were minor oddities, such as advancing ice while nearly broke and an early single-ice agenda lost to Inside Job.
Good pressure on HQ and R&D, with a sensible shuffle of two programs to steal Degree Mill and a quick win. Minor oddities were a redundant Self-modifying Code install and some idle credit clicks.

Clicked for credits up to 33 credits with no plan, never built a scoring remote, and left agendas in an HQ guarded only by Ping, where four were stolen. It then spent three turns repeatedly trying to trash the same DJ Fenris, three clicks at a time.

Built a reasonable economy and checked Archives often, picking up discarded agendas, and kept pressure on HQ through Anemone to win on turn 13. Some Archives runs and HQ runs that cost a net damage each time were marginal, but the overall plan was competent.

Clicked for credits up to 44 credits for over ten turns while the Corp scored Regenesis twice from a remote with one ice. Then, at 44 credits but only 5 cards against Jinteki, it ran the already-rezzed Anansi with no breaker a second time and was flatlined, which was clearly foreseeable.

Spent most turns clicking for credits with agendas in an HQ guarded only by Ping, and four were stolen. It never made a scoring remote and bled its 24 credits down to 2 by repeatedly paying to trash the same Daily Casts, three clicks at a time.

Efficient Weyland play: it fast-advanced Send a Message behind Border Control, used NGO Front and Government Subsidy for money, layered remote ice, and closed with SDS and Above the Law. There were no significant mistakes.

Left R&D unprotected for twelve turns against a Runner hitting it four times per turn, and lost two Fujii from it. Using AU Co.'s mill-and-draw every turn along with hand overflow then decked the Corp and lost the game.

Stayed tagged at 0 credits against NBN early and lost most of the grip to End of the Line, and also ran into an empty iced remote. It let Degree Mill, Orbital Superiority and the final Project Beale be advanced in Server 2 with little contest while spending turns on draws, Archives runs and clearing tags.

Clicked for credits up to 26 credits for ten turns with R&D and Archives open, letting the Runner trash assets and steal agendas freely. A late Oppo Research had no follow-up, and two clicks were spent trashing the same Dr. Nuka.

Spent the whole game at 0 credits running R&D 3-4 times a turn, re-accessing the same top card, and stayed tagged against NBN through two End of the Lines. It walked into the known Chekist Scion trap and won only because the Corp decked.

Spent many turns clicking for credits or running an empty Archives while the Corp scored three agendas from Server 1. When Pinhole Threading reached Send a Message, which would have been game-winning, it declined to steal despite having 15+ credits.

Against a Finality and sabotage deck it clicked for credits and drew instead of icing R&D, HQ and Archives, played IP Enforcement for no effect, and discarded into an open Archives. It lost on turn 5 without installing a single agenda.

Barely contested Server 1 while Send a Message and SDS were advanced behind one or two ice, then spent about ten turns on Archives runs, empty Pinhole Threadings and draws. It made one late facecheck and let Above the Law score for the win.

Very passive early, clicking for credits to 26 with a full hand and discarding each turn (including House of Knives into an open Archives). Later play was solid, scoring through Server 1 and Server 3 and closing with a Sting! flatline.

Scored three agendas sensibly behind Semak-samun, but discarded and milled agendas into a never-iced Archives. It then used Longevity Serum to trash its whole HQ and shuffled back non-agendas, handing the Runner a 9-point Archives run and the game.
Correctly hammered an unprotected R&D and Archives and won on turn 3. The only waste was repeating turn-1 R&D runs that could only re-access the same card.
